verification_level: FAST plus BATCH. One documentation-accuracy repair in src/provider/ecx_kem.rs (a SAFETY comment claimed ecx_key_check tolerated a NULL key while its body dereferences it); no behaviour changed. No unrepaired memory-safety defect, ABI regression, hidden obligation or unsafe-safe-Rust API was found.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the DSA keymgmt (generation context, import/export), ECDH and ECX key exchange, ECX DHKEM, the EC/SM2-to-blob encoder, the RSA/DSA PVK/MSBLOB encoder, the shared provider endecoder helpers, and the storemgmt DER/MSBLOB/PVK object decoders. src/evp/method_store.rs (the OSSL_METHOD_CONSTRUCT_METHOD registry boundary) was deferred again and src/provider/file_store_any2obj.rs substituted. Data classes: key-exchange shared secrets, KEM IKM/PRK/DH buffers and PVK/MSBLOB private-key bytes are SECRET_DATA/CLEANSING_REQUIRED; UKM is sensitive lifecycle state; OIDs, public keys and algorithm names are PUBLIC_DATA. No constant-time claim is made from source inspection.

documentation_corrections.change: The SAFETY comment said the key 'may be NULL'; the body dereferences (*ecx).privkey. The contract now states the KEM dispatch passes a live ECX_KEY at every init call, matching the authority and the actual precondition. Comment-only; no code or layout change.

retained_obligations.mechanism: keyexch/KEM dispatch dereferences (ecdh_freectx, ecdh_derive, ecx_freectx, ecx_derive, ecxkem_freectx, ecxkem_encapsulate/decapsulate)
retained_obligations.obligation: Each is an unsafe extern "C" function whose documented contract is the corresponding OSSL_FUNC_KEYEXCH_*/OSSL_FUNC_KEM_* dispatch contract; that contract supplies a non-NULL live context (and, for init/derive, a live key) created by newctx/init. The authority dereferences identically. No safe-Rust caller can reach these functions; the obligation is the C ABI's and is stated at each declaration.
retained_obligations.status: documented dispatch precondition, not a hidden obligation

retained_obligations.obligation: The field is documented as owned but is never assigned and therefore always NULL on this profile; the authority's ecx_kem.c also never assigns or frees ctx->propq. There is no allocation, so no leak and no cleansing obligation today. Recorded so a future assignment cannot silently acquire an unreleased allocation.
retained_obligations.status: documented inert field; authoritative behaviour preserved

retained_obligations.mechanism: private-key copies handed to callbacks (dsa_export OSSL_PARAM block; ossl_read_der DER block)
retained_obligations.obligation: dsa_export's OSSL_PARAM_BLD_to_param block and ossl_read_der's BUF_MEM data are released by the caller/authority through plain OSSL_PARAM_free/OPENSSL_free, exactly as the authority does; the private-key bytes they may carry are therefore not cleansed on those release paths. This is a preserved authority property, not a new conversion obligation; the owning key objects (DSA/EVP_PKEY/ECX_KEY) cleanse their own BIGNUMs through their destructors.
retained_obligations.status: authority-faithful; reported for the secret-lifetime ledger
